chunks: Or like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by waves, upon which are clouds; darknesses, some upon others. If he stretches out his hand, he can hardly see it. And for whom Allah has not made light, there is no light for him.

key_terms.بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍ: Deep sea (characterized by depth and lack of bottom)
key_terms.ظُلُمَاتٌ: Darknesses (plural, indicating layers or types of darkness)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor of darkness in the sea in Surah An-Nur?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (Ayat al-Nur) is often interpreted as describing the spiritual state of those devoid of the light of Imamate and divine knowledge, where layers of darkness represent increasing degrees of heedlessness. The progression from the sea to the waves to the clouds symbolizes the external distractions that obscure the inner heart, culminating in total spiritual blindness. This highlights the necessity of Allah's bestowal of Nur (light) through the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt for true guidance.
